edit_summary: Pass an fgets-style reader size that is one byte larger than the allocated line buffer.
root_cause: ini_parse_stream must pass the actual line-buffer capacity to the reader because fgets-style readers count the terminating NUL inside that size.
effect_path: A max-length line causes the reader callback to write up to max_line bytes plus a terminator into a buffer allocated for only max_line bytes before the parser computes strlen and dispatches line handling.
guard_p1: The active configuration uses the stack line buffer or a heap line buffer sized to max_line.
guard_p2: The input contains a physical line whose bytes before newline exactly fill the declared max_line capacity.
expected_crash: one-byte overflow from reader callback into the INI line buffer
hardness_reason: The bad size is passed through the generic reader abstraction, so the write occurs inside fgets or ini_reader_string before later parser state observes the overlong line; the positive and negative cases differ by one input byte.
naturalness_reason: Off-by-one mistakes in fgets-style size arguments are natural because the size includes the NUL terminator while parser constants are usually described as line lengths.
explanation: The stream parser owns a buffer of max_line bytes and gives that size to a callback with fgets semantics. Adding one lets a max-length physical line overflow the owned buffer by the terminator byte.
boundary_invariant: the reader size argument must be no larger than the actual line buffer capacity, including space for the terminating NUL
boundary_case: a line has exactly max_line bytes before newline or EOF under the configured line-buffer size
neighbor_case: the same line has at most max_line - 1 bytes before newline, leaving room for the terminator
oob_site_expected: fgets-compatible reader or ini_reader_string writes the terminating NUL one byte past line

edit_summary: Treat a length-delimited INI string buffer as if it had one extra readable byte.
root_cause: ini_parse_string_length must preserve the caller supplied byte length because the input need not have a trailing NUL byte.
effect_path: The inflated ctx.num_left crosses the ini_reader_string callback boundary, and the reader copies one byte past the caller buffer into the line buffer during normal stream parsing.
guard_p1: A caller uses ini_parse_string_length with a buffer whose valid extent is exactly length bytes and no extra sentinel byte is addressable.
guard_p2: The neighboring call supplies the same bytes plus an addressable sentinel byte after the range, or uses ini_parse_string on a NUL-terminated string.
hardness_reason: The length bug is introduced in the public length-delimited entry point and manifests later through the generic stream reader callback and line parser.
naturalness_reason: Confusing a byte length with space for a terminator is a realistic parser API boundary mistake.
explanation: The string-length entry point is specifically for bounded buffers. Adding one to the stored remaining count lets the internal fgets-like reader consume outside the caller-owned span.
boundary_invariant: ini_parse_string_ctx.num_left must equal the caller supplied length for length-delimited buffers
boundary_case: the valid input range ends exactly after length bytes with no accessible byte at string[length]
neighbor_case: the input is NUL-terminated and string[length] is accessible
oob_site_expected: ini_reader_string reads c = *ctx_ptr++ after ctx_num_left has been inflated

edit_summary: Leave the current section name uninitialized before parsing top-level name/value pairs.
root_cause: The parser state uses an empty section string to represent top-level keys before any section header has been parsed.
effect_path: A top-level name/value pair before the first section is dispatched through HANDLER with the uninitialized section buffer, and consumers such as INIReader::ValueHandler build map keys from that string.
guard_p1: The INI file begins with a valid name=value line before any [section] header.
guard_p2: The neighboring input starts with a [section] header, which initializes section through ini_strncpy0 before any handler receives it.
expected_crash: uninitialized stack bytes consumed as section string by parser callback
hardness_reason: The missing initialization occurs at parser setup, but the first meaningful use crosses parsing, name/value splitting, and the application handler callback.
naturalness_reason: Missing initialization of the default section state is a natural bug in small C parsers that support both top-level keys and explicit sections.
explanation: Top-level INI keys rely on section being an empty C string. Without the initializer, the handler receives stack contents as the section name.
init_site_expected: ini.c:112 section state initialization in ini_parse_stream
skip_init_predicate: a valid name=value line appears before the first section header
first_read_expected: HANDLER receives section, with INIReader::ValueHandler or another handler reading it as a C string
